categoryName: Sikh religious & Gurmat articles — dastar/turban fabric, patka, kanga, kara, kachhera, gutka/nitnem, prayer items, gurbani media, sarbloh utensils

skuLines.line: Turban fabric — full voile, cut piece
skuLines.examples: Mithat Full Voile; Sardar Exclusive full voile; Meri Dastar Full Voile; unbranded Amritsar (Hall Bazaar/Katra Ahluwalia) voile
skuLines.packSizes: 4 m / 5 m / 6 m / 7 m cut pieces; 60-100 m mill roll for institutional cutting
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes at school session start (Feb-Apr, Jul), Vaisakhi (Apr), Guru Nanak Parkash Purab (Nov), Parkash Purab Guru Gobind Singh (Dec/Jan) and wedding season (Nov-Feb)
skuLines.notes: Highest-rotation line in the whole category. Low weight / high value = ideal hill freight. Cotton voile needs 1-2 days to dry in the Jul-Sep Sirmaur monsoon, so a household keeps 4-6 pieces — monsoon demand goes UP, not down. Shade continuity is the whole game: a discontinued shade becomes dead stock, so buy depth in white/navy/black/kesri/royal blue and width only in fashion shades.

skuLines.line: Turban fabric — rubia voile / heavy rubia
skuLines.examples: Sikh Accessories Rubia Voile; Heavy Rubia Voile 5-6 m; Ehutty Rubia
skuLines.seasonality: Cold months (Oct-Feb) and formal/ceremonial occasions; heavier weave holds shape better in hill wind
skuLines.notes: Heavier = better shape retention, the standard for staff and formal dastar. Slower drying than full voile; humidity/mildew risk in stock — store off the floor on wooden racks in monsoon.

skuLines.line: Turban fabric — malmal / F74 premium fine cotton
skuLines.examples: Meri Dastar Premium Mal Mal F74; F74/F94 malmal 5-6 m; Supreme Voile
skuLines.seasonality: Summer (Apr-Jun) for breathability; gifting at Gurpurabs and weddings
skuLines.notes: The premium end the category needs so a wallet does not leak to Amritsar/Chandigarh. Ultra-fine 2x2 twisted cotton, snags easily — keep in sleeves, not open stacks.

skuLines.line: Turban fabric — bulk roll, cut-to-length by the metre
skuLines.examples: Mill roll voile in white/navy/kesri; institutional indent for hostels and the Academy uniform store
skuLines.packSizes: 60 m / 100 m rolls, cut to 4-7 m on demand
skuLines.seasonality: Bulk indents before session start (Feb-Apr) and Amrit-sanchar / Gurpurab camps
skuLines.marginBand: 12-22% on institutional, 35-50% when cut and retailed per piece
skuLines.notes: This is the margin engine: buy by the roll, sell by the cut piece. Also the only way to serve 5,000 residents on one hill road without stocking hundreds of finished pieces. Needs a cutting table, a metre stick and edge-finishing (turla) capability.

skuLines.line: Parna & dumalla cloth (short 3 m / long 8-11 m)
skuLines.examples: Parna plain & check 2.5-3 m; kesri / navy / black dumalla 8 m & 11 m; Taksali dumalla cloth
skuLines.packSizes: 2.5-3 m parna; 8 m / 9 m / 11 m dumalla
skuLines.seasonality: Parna year-round (work/sports/langar sewa); dumalla spikes Vaisakhi, Hola Mohalla (Mar), Gurpurabs, gatka events and Amrit sanchar
skuLines.notes: Parna is the everyday working head-cover for langar/farm/sports sewa and is bought casually — keep it near the counter. Dumalla is a low-frequency, high-ticket, occasion item; stock kesri and navy only.

skuLines.examples: Sikh Accessories Designer Printed; Mithat printed range; digital-print voile
skuLines.seasonality: Weddings (Nov-Feb), college functions, Vaisakhi, youth events
skuLines.notes: Fashion risk — buy narrow and shallow. Sells to the 18-25 university cohort, almost never to staff.

skuLines.examples: Sikh Accessories Small Size Patka 4 Knots; Big Size Patka 4 Knots; local Amritsar school patka in white/navy
skuLines.seasonality: Hard spike at session start (Feb-Apr) and after winter break (Jan-Feb); steady all year on replacement
skuLines.notes: The single highest-unit line in this category for a residential school of 5,000 — children lose, tear and outgrow patkas constantly. Stock ONLY the Academy uniform shades (white / navy) in depth; a wrong shade is unsellable here. Small, light, non-perishable — perfect for hill stocking depth.

skuLines.examples: Big Size Patka without Knots; senior-school patka; plain voile patka squares
skuLines.seasonality: Session start; year-round replacement
skuLines.notes: Bridge product between patka and full dastar for 13-16 year olds. Cut squares can be made in-store from bulk roll offcuts — near-zero waste.

skuLines.examples: Two Knots Cotton Patka; Two Knots Denim Patka; stretch sports patka
skuLines.seasonality: Sports season, gatka practice, winter (denim/heavier cotton)
skuLines.notes: Denim/2-knot is the everyday non-uniform patka for hostel and games time; more durable than voile, which matters where laundry is communal and rough.

skuLines.examples: Stocking cap; jooda cap; cotton under-cap
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; higher in winter (Nov-Feb) at 1,700 m altitude
skuLines.notes: Cheap, tiny, high-attach add-on to every patka/turban sale. Elastic perishes — rotate stock, do not hold more than 6 months.

skuLines.examples: Keski 2.5 m; under-dastar keski in white/navy/black
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; Amrit-sanchar camps spike it
skuLines.notes: Worn under the dastar and by Amritdhari women/girls; also the item newly-Amritdhari residents buy first. Cut from the same bulk roll as turban fabric.

skuLines.examples: Fifty plain white/black; fiftiyan card of 12; Mithat fifty
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round
skuLines.notes: Consumable — gets sweaty and discoloured, replaced far more often than the turban. Dozen packs are the right buying unit; sells at the counter as an impulse add-on.

skuLines.examples: Thatha plain black/white; velcro thatha; beard net
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round
skuLines.notes: Adult-only line, steady low-volume. Pair with beard oil/comb at the counter for basket build.

skuLines.examples: Steel salai; wooden baaj; dastar salai set
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round
skuLines.notes: Tiny, cheap, constantly lost — the classic 'they will drive 40 km if we do not have it' item. Zero spoilage, so keep 6-12 months of cover.

skuLines.line: Turban pins, dastar clips & safety-pin cards
skuLines.examples: Pag pin card; dastar brooch pin; steel safety pins No.2/No.3; velcro dastar clip
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; brooch/decorative pins spike at weddings and Gurpurabs
skuLines.notes: Rust in hill humidity — buy stainless/nickel-plated, not plain steel, and do not over-stock plain pins through the monsoon.

skuLines.examples: Kalgi steel & gold-plated; chand-tora; wedding sehra kalgi
skuLines.seasonality: Wedding season (Nov-Feb), Vaisakhi/Hola Mohalla nagar kirtan, gatka display
skuLines.notes: Occasion-only. Two or three SKUs is the whole shelf; gold-plating tarnishes in damp storage, keep in poly sleeves.

skuLines.examples: Kalaf/starch powder; Robin Blue / Ujala neel; Rangoli / Nirma-type fabric dye sachets; spray starch
skuLines.packSizes: 100 g / 500 g starch; 75 ml neel; 10 g dye sachets; 340 ml spray
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; heaviest in monsoon (Jul-Sep) when whites go dull, and before Gurpurabs
skuLines.notes: Overlaps the home-care lane but is bought as a dastar accessory — merchandise it beside the turban fabric, not with detergents. Dye sachets let a resident refresh a faded uniform-shade turban instead of buying new.

skuLines.examples: Plain steel kara 6/7/8 cm; solid chakri steel kara with brass line; Khalsa Store plain kada
skuLines.packSizes: Single; retail set of 5 (buying unit from Amritsar)
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; gift spikes at Gurpurabs, Vaisakhi, birthdays, Amrit sanchar
skuLines.notes: Buying unit from Amritsar wholesale is a set of 5 — size ladder (small/medium/large wrist) matters more than design. Non-perishable, no shrinkage risk, ideal hill stock.

skuLines.examples: Pure Sarabloh Kara medium weight (₹320-350 on Amritsar retail sites); slim chakri sarbloh; heavy sarbloh
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; Amrit sanchar and Vaisakhi spikes
skuLines.notes: Iron RUSTS — the one real hill-humidity constraint in this category. Oil-wipe on receipt, store with silica/oiled paper, and never hold monsoon stock in an unsealed carton. Amritdhari residents specifically ask for sarbloh, not steel; some also want it for iron intake.

skuLines.examples: Laser-engraved kara (₹750-850); Gurmukhi Mool Mantar engraved (₹395-1,200); brass-line and silver-work kara (₹1,900)
skuLines.seasonality: Gift season — Gurpurabs (Nov, Dec/Jan), Vaisakhi, birthdays, convocation/farewell (Mar-Apr)
skuLines.notes: The gifting tier and the best margin in the kakaar shelf. Name/Mool Mantar engraving can be attached as a paid service (see adjacent services).

skuLines.examples: Newborn baby kara set of 5 (₹475-600); kids 4-5 cm steel kara; baby sarbloh kara
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round — birth gifting has no season
skuLines.notes: Married staff families with babies are a defined cohort here; the newborn kara is the first purchase and travels with a gift. Small sizes are easy to lose in the display — keep on a card, not loose.

skuLines.examples: Sikh kanga small pocket 5 cm; large 9 cm wooden kanga; steel-plate-back kanga; kanga with mini kirpan
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; session start for students
skuLines.notes: Cheapest of the five kakaars and the most frequently replaced — teeth snap, kids lose them. Wood swells/warps in monsoon damp: keep sealed, avoid the cheapest unfinished stock. Pack-of-3 is the right family SKU.

skuLines.examples: Kachera set of 3 (₹420-540 on Amritsar retail); Taksali kachera set of 3 (₹960); plain cotton kachhera
skuLines.packSizes: Single; set of 3 (standard buying and selling unit)
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; session start and Amrit sanchar spikes
skuLines.notes: Size ladder is the stock-out risk, not design — hold S through XXL. Sold in 3s; a resident buys 3-6 at a time because communal laundry turnaround is slow. Taksali (longer) variant is a distinct ask, keep 2-3 pieces.

skuLines.examples: Kids kachera 20-26 inch waist; school-size kachhera set of 3
skuLines.seasonality: Session start (Feb-Apr); replacement year-round as children grow
skuLines.notes: Growth-driven repeat purchase in a 5-18 residential school. Waist-size ladder must be complete or the parent goes to town.

skuLines.examples: Kirpan 6 inch (Sikh Accessories ID-004/208); 3 inch pocket kirpan; steel kirpan with sheath
skuLines.seasonality: Amrit sanchar camps, Vaisakhi, Gurpurabs
skuLines.notes: Legally clear for Sikhs to keep and wear (kirpan is exempted under the Arms Act / Art. 25 Explanation I) — no arms licence for a religious kirpan; still keep it behind the counter, not on open self-service display, in a school township, and do not sell loose blades to children. Blade rusts: oiled sheath, check stock in monsoon.

skuLines.examples: 9 inch kirpan; Siri Sahib with velvet sheath; Shree Amritsar Sword ceremonial kirpan; wedding kirpan
skuLines.seasonality: Weddings (Nov-Feb), Amrit sanchar, nagar kirtan, gatka display, gifting to Gurdwara
skuLines.notes: Very low velocity, high ticket — 2-4 pieces is the whole assortment, or order-to-indent. Same legal position as above; keep a sale register entry and never display within reach of students.

skuLines.examples: Khalsa Store gatra 1" ₹149-399, 1.5" ₹149-599; designer gatra ₹699; kids gatra in black/blue/kesri
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; Amrit sanchar and Vaisakhi spikes
skuLines.notes: Wears out and stains faster than the kirpan — the repeat half of the kirpan sale. Stock black, navy and kesri; skip fashion colours.

skuLines.examples: Kamarkasa plain; hazooria white/kesri; khajana waist belt
skuLines.seasonality: Amrit sanchar, sewa duty, nagar kirtan, gatka, Gurpurabs
skuLines.notes: Bought by Amritdhari residents and sewadars; hazooria in white also moves as a Gurdwara-sewa item. Two SKUs each is enough.

skuLines.examples: Kara + kanga + kachhera + small kirpan + gatra + keski, bundled; 'panj kakaar' gift box
skuLines.packSizes: Single bundle (sized S/M/L); institutional pack of 10-25 for camps
skuLines.seasonality: Hard spike at Amrit-sanchar camps (typically Vaisakhi Apr, Gurpurab Nov-Jan and camp weeks); near zero between
skuLines.notes: A township with an Academy and a University runs organised Amrit sanchar — a pre-built bundle is a genuine convenience and a real basket lift. Made entirely from components already stocked, so it carries no extra inventory risk. Ask the Gurdwara/Trust office for camp dates and indent ahead.

skuLines.examples: Nitnem gutka pocket (Singh Brothers / Bhai Chattar Singh Jiwan Singh, Amritsar); Budha Dal nitnem gutka; Dharam Prachar Committee nitnem
skuLines.seasonality: Session start, Amrit sanchar, Gurpurabs; gifting Nov-Jan
skuLines.marginBand: 20-30% (publisher trade discount is 10-25% off a printed MRP; margin is capped)
skuLines.notes: Handle with the respect the item requires — clean high shelf, cloth-covered, never on the floor or under other goods; no polybag stacking with grocery. Print MRP limits margin, so it is a footfall/duty line, not a profit line. Damp swells paper in monsoon: keep sealed and off outer walls.

skuLines.line: Gutka Sahib — Sundar Gutka / all-banis, large print, hardbound
skuLines.examples: Sundar Gutka (all nitnem + extra banis); Panj Granthi; Das Granthi; large-print gutka for elderly
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; gifting at Gurpurabs and retirement/farewell
skuLines.notes: Large print is specifically an elderly-cohort need and is the version they cannot substitute with a phone app. Stock at least one 18-point large-print SKU.

skuLines.examples: Sukhmani Sahib gutka; Japji Sahib gutka; Jaap Sahib; Chaupai Sahib; Asa Di Vaar
skuLines.packSizes: Single; pack of 10-25 for a sehaj-path/Sukhmani sewa group
skuLines.seasonality: Sukhmani Sahib path groups (weekly/monthly), Gurpurabs, house functions, Poornmashi/Sangrand
skuLines.notes: Sukhmani sewa societies buy 10-40 identical copies at once for a group path — the one line here with genuine bulk demand. Keep a carton, not three pieces.

skuLines.line: Gutka — Roman English / Hindi transliteration & translation
skuLines.examples: Nitnem Roman English gutka; Nitnem Hindi gutka; steel-plate Roman-script nitnem; English translation banis
skuLines.seasonality: Session start; year-round
skuLines.notes: Real demand in a national/international-intake residential school and university: non-Punjabi-reading students and non-Punjabi staff. Roman and Devanagari script versions are separate SKUs, both needed.

skuLines.line: Gutka rumala / cover / pouch / steel-plate cover
skuLines.examples: Embroidered gutka rumala; velvet gutka cover; steel-plate gutka cover; zip gutka pouch with strap
skuLines.seasonality: Attaches to every gutka sale; gifting at Gurpurabs
skuLines.notes: Best-margin attachment in the books shelf and religiously expected — never sell a gutka without offering one. Waterproof/steel covers matter here: students walk to the Gurdwara in heavy monsoon rain.

skuLines.examples: Wooden folding rehal; carved rehal; small palki-style gutka stand; sheesham rehal
skuLines.seasonality: Gurpurabs, house-warming, gifting, new hostel prayer rooms
skuLines.notes: Bought once per household/prayer room, so demand is thin but non-substitutable. Wood + monsoon = warping; buy seasoned sheesham, keep flat.

skuLines.examples: Wool/cotton knotted mala; sandalwood 108-bead mala; sarbloh/steel bead mala; tulsi-alternative wooden mala
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; Amrit sanchar, Gurpurabs, elderly gifting
skuLines.notes: Cheap wool malas move as an everyday item and as camp giveaways; sandalwood is the gift tier. Iron/sarbloh malas rust like the kara — same storage rule.

skuLines.line: Pocket Gurbani cards, Mool Mantar cards & wall plaques
skuLines.examples: Laminated Mool Mantar card; Japji Sahib pocket card; 'Ik Onkar' wall plaque; Nitnem summary card
skuLines.packSizes: Single; card of 10 for school/hostel distribution
skuLines.seasonality: Session start; Gurpurabs; camp giveaways
skuLines.notes: Near-zero cost, near-zero risk, high margin, and institutions buy them in hundreds for hostels and classrooms. Good counter-side impulse.

skuLines.examples: Gurmukhi Qaida (Singh Brothers, ~₹150 MRP); Punjabi Paenti board book; Gurmukhi writing/tracing practice books; Punjabi grammar for classes 1-5
skuLines.seasonality: Very hard spike at session start (Mar-Jul); flat otherwise
skuLines.notes: In a Gurmukhi-medium-friendly residential school this is a genuine must-stock and it also sells to staff families teaching toddlers at home. Coordinate the indent with the Academy's book list or the whole lot dead-stocks after July.

skuLines.line: Sikh children's story, activity & colouring books
skuLines.examples: Sahibzade story books; Ten Gurus illustrated set; Sikh colouring books (sikhcolouring-type); Punjabi folktale picture books; sticker/activity books
skuLines.seasonality: Session start, Gurpurabs, Shaheedi Jor Mela / Sahibzade Shaheedi week (late Dec), gifting and prize distribution (Mar-Apr)
skuLines.notes: The Academy and hostels buy these as prizes and library refills — an institutional line, not just a retail one. Late-December Sahibzade commemoration is a reliable annual spike here.

skuLines.line: Gurmat literature — Rehat Maryada, steek/teeka, Sikh history, Sant literature
skuLines.examples: Sikh Rehat Maryada (SGPC); Guru Granth Sahib Darpan / steek volumes; Bhai Vir Singh titles; Sikh history (Singh Brothers, Amritsar); Kalgidhar Trust / Baru Sahib publications
skuLines.seasonality: Gurpurabs, seminars/Gurmat camps, convocation gifting
skuLines.notes: A university on campus makes this defensible where it would not be in a village store. Buy shallow across many titles, deep in none; multi-volume sets on indent only. Publisher trade terms (Singh Brothers, Bhai Chattar Singh Jiwan Singh, SGPC) cap the margin.

skuLines.examples: SGPC Nanakshahi calendar; Khalsa Heera Jantri; Punjabi jantri wall + pocket; desk Nanakshahi calendar
skuLines.seasonality: Sharp, short window — Dec-Jan and again around Chet/Vaisakhi (Mar-Apr); worthless after
skuLines.notes: Pure seasonal — buy once, sell out, do not repeat. Every household, hostel office and department wants one, so institutional bundles move first. Dead stock after March, so under-buy rather than over-buy.

skuLines.line: Rumala Sahib — daily cotton / satin set
skuLines.examples: Cotton rumala sahib 50x44in + 2 palkas; satin daily rumala; Anmol Rumala / Sikh Rumala Centre sets
skuLines.seasonality: Gurpurabs (Nov, Dec/Jan), Vaisakhi, Sangrand/Poornmashi, birthdays, anniversaries, death anniversaries — sewa gifting has a calendar
skuLines.notes: Residents buy this to OFFER at the Gurdwara, so demand is event-linked, not consumption-linked. Cotton for summer/monsoon, heavier for winter, per convention. Bulky and crushable — the one line in this category with real hill-freight volume cost.

skuLines.line: Rumala Sahib — velvet / hand-embroidered / premium sewa set
skuLines.examples: Velvet embroidered rumala sahib; khadi-silk / banarasi brocade rumala; hand-kaarigari rumala (₹5,000-15,000 on Amritsar wholesale)
skuLines.seasonality: Major Gurpurabs, weddings, memorial sewa
skuLines.notes: Big-ticket, slow-moving, capital-heavy — carry 2-3 pieces as display and sell the rest on catalogue/indent from Amritsar (Katra Ahluwalia). Velvet mildews at 1,700 m in the monsoon; do not hold through Jul-Sep.

skuLines.examples: Chandoa sahib with patti; embroidered chandni; velvet chandoa
skuLines.seasonality: Gurpurabs, new prayer-room setup, Gurdwara renovation
skuLines.notes: Indent-only. Bought by the institution or as a large sewa offering — sell from a catalogue, do not stock.

skuLines.examples: Chaur sahib small/medium; steel-handle chaur; silver-plated handle chaur
skuLines.seasonality: Gurpurabs; new prayer rooms; replacement when worn
skuLines.notes: Needed by every prayer room and hostel Gurdwara on campus; one or two SKUs plus indent. Keep dust-sleeved.

skuLines.line: Nishan Sahib chola cloth + khanda finial
skuLines.examples: Kesri nishan sahib chola (assorted heights); khanda top steel/brass; nishan sahib rope & cover
skuLines.seasonality: Vaisakhi (Apr) is the traditional chola-change; also Gurpurabs and after storm damage
skuLines.notes: Institutional line — the Trust/Gurdwara changes cholas on a calendar, and hill wind and monsoon shred them faster than in the plains, so replacement is more frequent here than a plains store would plan for. Ask the Gurdwara office for the annual indent.

skuLines.line: Sarbloh utensils — batta, thali, glass, karshi
skuLines.examples: Sarabloh batta (bowl); 5-division sarbloh thali 11x14in; sarbloh glass; 3"/4" sarbloh karshi (ladle)
skuLines.seasonality: Amrit sanchar, Gurpurabs, gifting; year-round base
skuLines.notes: Specifically asked for by Amritdhari residents (and by anyone who wants iron in the diet). Heavy — the worst weight-to-value ratio in the category on a 30-50 km hill road, so buy in one consolidated annual/half-yearly lot. RUSTS: needs oil-wipe on arrival and before monsoon; sell with a one-line care note or it comes back as a complaint.

skuLines.examples: Sarabloh karahi (karah prasad); sarbloh patila; large degh vessel; iron tawa
skuLines.seasonality: Gurpurabs, Akhand Path / house functions, langar sewa
skuLines.notes: Bought once, lasts decades — one or two sizes only. Heavy freight; combine with the sarbloh utensil lot. Also bought for domestic karah prasad, so keep one small 8-10 inch karahi as the moving SKU.

skuLines.line: Desi ghee jyot, cotton batti & jyot oil
skuLines.examples: Shubhkart Darshana Pooja Ghee; Shubhkart ghee diya batti (~₹86); cotton phool batti 100 pc (~₹15); long-burn jyot wicks; mustard/til jyot oil
skuLines.packSizes: Ghee 100-500 ml; wicks 100-500 pc; oil 200 ml-1 L
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes Gurpurabs, Bandi Chhor Divas / Diwali (Oct-Nov), Sangrand, Poornmashi, house paths
skuLines.notes: Genuinely fast-moving and cheap to stock; already a q-commerce staple in the plains (Blinkit/BigBasket 'pooja needs'), so residents know the brands and prices. Note the institutional convention: some Sikh sangats use jyot and some do not — follow what the campus Gurdwara actually does before buying depth.

skuLines.examples: Hari Darshan De-luxe Dhoop (₹24/20 pc); Mangaldeep 3-in-1 agarbatti (₹54/72 pc); Cycle sandal agarbatti; Homelites matchbox (₹10/5 units); dhoop cones
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; Gurpurabs, Diwali/Bandi Chhor (Oct-Nov), Sangrand
skuLines.notes: Overlaps the household lane but is bought as a prayer-room item — merchandise it with prayer goods. Absorbs moisture and loses fragrance in monsoon: buy small, frequent lots, keep sealed. No tobacco-adjacent SKUs on this campus.

skuLines.examples: Plain cotton head rumal kesri/navy/white; printed Ik Onkar rumal; Gurdwara-entry bandana pack
skuLines.packSizes: Single; bundle of 12-50 for the Gurdwara entrance
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes at Gurpurabs and visitor/parents' days
skuLines.notes: Every visitor, every guest, every parents' day needs one, and the Gurdwara/reception buys them in dozens. Cheap, light, tiny — the single easiest institutional line to hold in depth on a hill.

skuLines.examples: Plain cotton chunni 2.25 m in uniform white/navy; chiffon dupatta; school-shade chunni; Amritsari cotton chunni
skuLines.cohort: students | university | staff | families (girls and women)
skuLines.seasonality: Session start (Feb-Apr); year-round replacement; Gurpurabs
skuLines.notes: The female half of head-covering demand and every bit as non-optional as the patka — stock the Academy uniform shades in depth. Overlaps the clothing lane; keep the uniform shades with Gurmat/head-cover goods so a parent finds patka and chunni in one place.

skuLines.examples: Phulkari dupatta hand/machine; Patiala phulkari stole; phulkari shawl for winter gifting
skuLines.seasonality: Weddings (Nov-Feb), Lohri/Maghi (Jan), Vaisakhi, gifting and farewell (Mar-Apr), winter
skuLines.notes: Gift/occasion line, not a religious requirement — keep it thin (4-6 pieces) and treat it as a wedding-season buy. Also the natural gift-to-take-home for visiting parents.

skuLines.line: Guru photo frames, posters & Sikh decor
skuLines.examples: Guru Nanak Dev Ji framed photo; Ten Gurus poster set; Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) frame & 3D replica; Mool Mantar wall frame; laminated wall posters
skuLines.packSizes: Single; poster sets of 5-10; sizes 8x10 to 16x24 in
skuLines.seasonality: Gurpurabs (Nov, Dec/Jan), Vaisakhi, new-quarter/hostel-room setup at session start, gifting
skuLines.notes: High margin, no expiry, but glass frames break on a hill road — prefer laminated/acrylic or unframed prints and frame locally. Every new staff quarter and hostel room is a sale.

skuLines.line: Khanda / Ik Onkar pendants, keychains, car hangings, stickers
skuLines.examples: Steel khanda pendant with chain; Ik Onkar keychain; khanda car hanging; 'Waheguru' car/laptop sticker; dashboard khanda
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; Gurpurabs, Vaisakhi, gifting, bus/taxi owners
skuLines.notes: Best-margin impulse block in the category and the classic pocket-money purchase for a 12-18 year old. Card them at the counter. Cheap plating corrodes in damp — avoid the lowest tier.

skuLines.line: Kesh care — reetha/shikakai/amla wash, kesh oil, beard oil & brush
skuLines.examples: Reetha-shikakai-amla hair wash powder; Dabur Amla / Kesh King oil; sarson (mustard) hair oil; herbal beard oil; wooden beard brush
skuLines.packSizes: 100-500 g powder; 100-300 ml oil; single brush
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; oil demand up in winter (Nov-Feb) hill dryness
skuLines.notes: Overlaps the personal-care lane, but uncut kesh makes this a Gurmat-specific need — long-hair volumes are far higher here than a normal store plans, and traditional reetha/shikakai (no-sulphate) buyers are a distinct, loyal segment. Merchandise beside kanga and thatha.

skuLines.line: Gatka gear — soti, farri, chakkar, sash
skuLines.examples: Gatka soti (stick); farri (shield); chakkar; gatka team sash/baana belt; practice gloves
skuLines.seasonality: Hola Mohalla (Mar), Vaisakhi, school sports/gatka meets, Gurpurab display teams
skuLines.notes: Only worth stocking because the Academy actually teaches gatka — sell to the coach/team on indent rather than holding retail stock. Wooden soti splits in damp; store dry.

skuLines.line: Gurbani player / Nitnem radio & preloaded media

skuLines.notes: Buy for the calendar and clear it; unsold festival decor sits a full year. Hostels, departments and the Gurdwara all decorate, so institutional demand front-loads it — take indents two weeks before each Gurpurab. Cheap LED strings fail in damp; buy a step above the cheapest.

trends2026: Pre-tied and velcro/ready-to-wear dastars and patkas are the fastest-growing sub-segment — driven exactly by hostel/boarding routines where 5-18 year olds have minutes to get ready; brands and D2C sellers now list 'ready turban' as a distinct category alongside cloth.

Turban fabric has genuinely brandified: Mithat, Meri Dastar, Sardar Exclusive and Sikh Accessories now sell shade-coded ranges (1,000+ shades) with online shade cards, so buyers arrive naming a shade code and a fabric grade (Full Voile / Rubia / F74 / Supreme) instead of 'white 5 metre'. A store that cannot match a named shade loses the sale.

Quick-dry, wrinkle-resistant and no-starch 'wash-and-wear' voile blends are being pushed for exactly the humid/monsoon problem — relevant at Baru Sahib, where drying time is the real constraint on how many turbans a resident must own.

Sarbloh is being re-marketed as a wellness product (dietary iron), not only a Nihang/Taksali requirement — sarbloh water bottles, tumblers and batta sets are appearing in mainstream Sikh e-commerce, widening the buyer from Amritdhari-only to health-conscious staff.

Phone apps (SikhiToTheMax, iGurbani, Nanakshahi calendar apps) have flattened youth demand for printed gutkas and paper jantris, while ELDERLY demand for large-print gutkas and standalone Gurbani radio players is holding or growing — the assortment is splitting by age, not shrinking.

Gurbani player hardware has moved up a generation: Bluetooth, USB-C, 1,700+ hours preloaded, FM/AM/AUX/SD, sold on Amazon.in at ₹1,000-4,000 — plus a healthy aftermarket in preloaded SD cards/pen drives, which is the high-margin half.

Rumala Sahib sewa is going online (Anmol Rumala, Sikh Rumala Centre, buyrumalasahib.com, My Pooja Box) with wholesale pricing, order-and-deliver-to-Gurdwara flows and lighter 'eco' cotton sets replacing heavy velvet — a local store must compete on same-day availability and on a receipt for the donor, not on price.

Sikh-identity merchandise for the 15-25 cohort (Ik Onkar / Khanda / Fateh print tees, laptop and car stickers, minimalist steel khanda pendants) is now a real impulse block, and 'mini Singh' newborn gift sets (baby kara + patka + Ik Onkar) have become a standard gifting SKU.

Q-commerce (Blinkit, Zepto, BigBasket) has taken over the generic prayer consumables — ghee diya batti, wicks, dhoop, agarbatti, matchboxes at ₹10-90 — and residents now know those price points, but almost NO Sikh-specific SKU (patka, kara, gutka, gatra, sarbloh) is available on 10-minute delivery, and none of it reaches Baru Sahib anyway. The Gurmat assortment is structurally protected here; the consumables are the price-benchmarked part.
adjacentServices: Cut-to-length turban service off the bulk roll, with edge-finishing/turla stitching and hemming — turns a 12-22% roll margin into a 35-50% piece margin and removes the need to stock hundreds of finished pieces on a hill.

Dastar-bandi (turban tying) training for boys moving from patka to dastar, and a paid tying service before weddings, convocations and Gurpurabs — the highest-trust service a Gurmat counter can offer in a school township.
Turban starching (kalaf), pressing, whitening and colour-matched dyeing/re-dyeing to the Academy uniform shade — solves the monsoon dullness problem and creates a weekly repeat visit.

Kara engraving (name, Mool Mantar, Ik Onkar) and kirpan polishing/sharpening; sarbloh rust-removal and oiling service before and after the monsoon — all three are pure-labour, high-margin, and impossible to get within 30-50 km.

Gutka binding/repair (jild) plus a respectful collection point for worn gutkas, pothis and saroops for agan-bhet through the campus Gurdwara — a duty-of-care service, not a profit line, and it is the reason a household trusts the counter with religious goods at all.

Rumala Sahib and Chandoa sewa desk: catalogue ordering from Amritsar (Katra Ahluwalia / Hall Bazaar), delivery to the Gurdwara on a chosen date (birthday, anniversary, barsi), and a receipt in the donor's name — captures a high-ticket sale without holding velvet stock through the monsoon.

Institutional indent supply to the Academy uniform store, hostels, the University and the Gurdwara office: patka, chunni, head rumal, nishan sahib chola, class-set qaidas, prize books, Gurpurab decoration — calendar-driven purchase orders that de-risk almost every seasonal line in this category.

Amrit-sanchar camp kitting: pre-built 5-kakaar bundles in sized packs, quoted per candidate and delivered to the camp — built from components already in stock, so it adds margin without adding inventory.

Gurbani player setup service — loading SD cards and pen drives with Nitnem, Sukhmani Sahib, kirtan and katha, and setting up Gurbani apps on elders' phones; also the courier RMA path for any device that fails, which is what makes electronics sellable at this distance.

Newborn and farewell gift hampers for staff families (baby kara set + patka + Ik Onkar pendant; gutka + rumala + kara for convocation) — pre-wrapped, priced, and available the same day, which is the whole value on a campus 40 km from a market.
